items.title: Ernest Poree Interview, 1975-10-16
items.q: And I used to go to him and take lessons from him.

ctx.x: So you weren't too terribly far from the Humber's house? No, I wasn't too far from that. You could walk there if you had to walk back.

That's right. I could walk back. I lived more and after we moved off to Constantinople, I lived more and general Taylor's. Right where that was right around the corner. I wasn't too far away. And what about the banjo? How did you learn the banjo? Well, I have a few ideas. I had a friend of mine, Nathaniel Morris. He was a great banjoist. Who? Nathaniel Morris. He has a son that's great, two sons, at least great drummers. One of them they call, what that boy, I can't call his name. He's up in St. Louisville. He's…
How did you really get into playing? Was it mainly through the lessons? Did you work out some of your own ideas? How do you do that?
